disclosures.name: TestMorePanic
disclosures.reason: The test re-execs the binary and matches the child's panic/Goexit report against Go's text with an unanchored regexp. Neither case reaches Go's crash: the host contains a test-body or cleanup panic (a record, the one test failed, the run continues) where Go's tRunner reaches doPanic, the runtime prints the panic chain and the binary exits 2. Case 2 (issue 48515, t.Run during t.Cleanup) passes, but only on a substring: the host refuses with Go's "testing: t.Run called during t.Cleanup", and the regexp finds "panic: testing: t.Run called during t.Cleanup" inside the host's own "cleanup panic: ..." record, where Go prints "panic: testing: t.Run called during t.Cleanup [recovered, repanicked]" and crashes. Case 1 (issue 48502, runtime.Goexit in t.Cleanup after a panic) fails: the host reports the cleanup's Goexit as an infrastructure-error row with CLR stack traces, where Go prints "panic: die" over a tab-indented "panic: test executed panic(nil) or runtime.Goexit". Both retire when the host reproduces Go's doPanic and its crash-report chain, with the test pipeline re-launched so the tail stays measured.

disclosures.name: TestAllocsPerRun
disclosures.reason: Exact-count AllocsPerRun asserts (want 1 for each of five `new(T)` closures). In Go too, `global = new(T)` escapes into `any` and costs one malloc (allocs_test.go:9-20). The four legs with an unmanaged T print 2 (`AllocsPerRun(100, alloc complex128) = 2, want 1`), a count by construction (each run mints a counted box, so testing.cs:750 takes the count path); the new(*byte) leg reads 1 per run (100 go2cs-runtime object allocations, 5,600 bytes, over 100 runs, Release with tiering off, the same at go1.26.10 on windows and linux, a lower bound) and passes. The extra object is the one Go never allocates: for an unmanaged T the managed pointer needs address-stable storage, because through the interface it is reachable by reflect and unsafe as an integer address. Go's non-moving heap gives that for free; the CLR's compacting GC does not, so ж<T> over an unmanaged T allocates an eager pinnable T[1] slot beside the box (golib/ж.StandardBox.cs:61-67; AllocationCounter.cs:39-42). The two nameable alternatives fail. (a) A pointer that is the pinned array (the box pinning itself) roots itself through the strong pinned handle and can never die, a structural leak; and a lazily created slot breaks heap()'s ref alias, because storage handed out by ref must never migrate. (b) Whole-program analysis selecting a slot-free box kind is not possible because the pointer flows into `any`, where every later use is outside the analysis. The new(*byte) leg is the control: a managed element type needs no slot and reads 1.

disclosures.name: TestTBHelper
disclosures.reason: Applies to the default Release configuration; a Debug build passes this test. The test checks the file and line that t.Helper attribution reports for each call in a chain of helpers. Go reports helperfuncs_test.go:86 and :87 for `genericHelper[float64](t, "GenericFloat64")` and `genericIntHelper(t, "GenericInt")`; the converted test reports :84 for both, the line of the statement before them. Those two calls are the only ones in the test whose string argument the converted code reads through a hoisted literal's read-only accessor (the form introduced at 5bf0fcb694), right after reading the closure-captured `t`. In the optimized build the JIT keeps no IL boundary for either statement, so both calls report the offset of the statement before them, while every call that passes a plain literal reports its own line, and a Debug build reports all of them correctly. The runtime cannot tell the two frames apart: both report one IL offset, and the callee as the open generic definition `genericHelper[G]` (the runtime reports a generic method by its definition), so only their native offsets differ, and no in-process map ties a native offset to a call. Measured on windows/amd64, Release: converters at 7072ef5904 and 1dacbdf4b6 validate this test, and 5bf0fcb694 fails it; on linux, Release with tiering off, at 8aaa6cebc8 both frames read IL 0xE9. Retires when an emission shape keeps both statements' boundaries in the optimized method.
disclosures.history: structural, disclosed 2026-11-01 under COORD's ruling (C) on G's seat #45 follow-up finding; option (B) is the post-hop retirement. Found when the #45 follow-up (d9da4a7f11) let testing convert again: its bank-act row read TestTBHelper C# fail, Go pass, with helperfuncs_test.go 86 and 87 reported as :84. BISECT, windows Release, one tree (c5a4637bba), one act, the #45 follow-up fix cherry-picked onto each arm because every converter after #45 refuses testing without it: 1dacbdf4b6 (batch 109) validates 83 + 2; 5bf0fcb694 (batch 110, seat #53, the hoist-mode `ref readonly` literal accessor) fails exactly TestTBHelper; 7072ef5904 (batch 98) validates. -test-config Debug at d9da4a7f11 validates 83 + 2. The emission: at 5bf0fcb694 the test reads `genericFloat64ˢ` and `genericIntˢ` through `private static ref readonly @string genericFloat64ˢ => ref genericFloat64ˢᵇ;`, and only the two calls passing them misreport. RETIREMENT (B): #55's caller-line resolver maps a call through an inlined accessor to its own line, post-hop, with a census of the standard library's caller-line readers (log Lshortfile, testing.Helper). Option (A), a -tests-only plain-field emission, was refused under the owner's standing ruling of 2026-09-28 (ledger e15a841635): visible emission is never changed to satisfy a test that asserts diagnostic-only output. S8 (P1, 2026-11-05, COORD ruling (a)): option (B) was built and cannot retire this test. Linux, Release, tiering off, at 8aaa6cebc8: the GenericFloat64 frame and the GenericInt frame (a delegate call) both report testHelper IL 0xE9, the recoverHelper statement, and StackFrame.GetMethod returns the generic definition for both, so the capture records them as one call site; a C# probe reproduces it (both report caller IL 0x1E and GHelper[G], native offsets 0x96 and 0xC0). The JIT keeps no IL boundary for either statement: their native code begins at the previous call's return address with no mapping of their own. Ranking frames by native offset was refused: it needs both calls to have run, and the test reads the GenericFloat64 line first. Probe readings for an emission fix: a by-value accessor (`@string genericFloat64ˢ => genericFloat64ˢᵇ;`) fixed the probe but the real method still read :84 for both; JitNoForwardSub=1 and a NoInlining accessor changed nothing. S8's step-over (a lone direct call of a non-generic callee) refuses a generic callee for exactly this reason.
